title: String Quartet No. 8 in C minor
hook: A composer’s portrait of himself, written in three days, signed with his own initials in notes.

painting.title: The Ruins of the Old Kreuzkirche in Dresden
painting.pairingNote: Dresden’s great church lies in ruins after a bombardment in 1760; exactly two hundred years later Shostakovich wrote this quartet near the city, among the ruins of another war.

facts: Shostakovich wrote the quartet in three days, 12 to 14 July 1960, at Gohrisch, near Dresden. He had gone to East Germany to write music for a film about the bombing of Dresden in the Second World War.

It came shortly after he had joined the Communist Party, which he did reluctantly. The printed score is dedicated “to the victims of fascism and war”. To his friend Isaak Glikman he wrote, bitterly, that he had written it in memory of its author. Friends said he thought of it as his own epitaph.

Every movement is built on his musical signature, [[dsch|DSCH]]: the notes D, E-flat, C, B, his initials in German spelling. The quartet is also full of quotations from his own earlier works, like a life passing before his eyes.
The five movements are played without a break: three slow movements frame two fast ones.
The story goes that when the Borodin Quartet played it to him at his home in Moscow, he buried his head in his hands and wept, and the four players quietly packed up and left.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a lament (I), a fury (II), a ghostly waltz (III), knocks and memories (IV), a farewell (V).

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: Four slow notes in the cello, Shostakovich’s signature, taken up by each instrument in turn. A grey, still lament, with fragments of his earlier music drifting through it.

mainIdeas.description: [[dsch|DSCH]]: four notes, close together, turning back on themselves. They run through the whole quartet.
The movement quotes his First Symphony, written when he was 19, and his Fifth.

stops.hear: The cello alone, low and slow: four notes; then the viola, the second violin and the first violin enter one by one with the same notes
stops.happening: The signature, in a [[fugato|fugato]]

stops.hear: The first violin, high and exposed, plays a different, angular phrase
stops.happening: A memory of his First Symphony

stops.hear: A long, drifting violin melody over chords that hardly move; a low note is held underneath
stops.happening: The lament deepens over a [[pedal-note|pedal note]]

stops.hear: The four notes return in the lower instruments
stops.happening: The signature again

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The sound thins to a held note, which breaks straight into the next movement
stops.happening: No pause. The quartet runs on

movements.heading: Allegro molto
movements.summary: A sudden explosion. All four instruments attack at top speed and full volume. In the middle, a wild, dance-like tune from his Second Piano Trio, a work written in 1944 that draws on Jewish folk music.

stops.hear: Loud, fast, hard-driven chords and runs from all four players
stops.happening: The violence breaks out

stops.hear: The first violin screams out a frantic dance tune over thumping chords
stops.happening: The theme from the Second Piano Trio

stops.hear: The signature notes hammered by all four players together
stops.happening: The signature in [[unison|unison]], at full force

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: The music cuts off and slides straight into the waltz
stops.happening: Into the next movement

movements.heading: Allegretto
movements.summary: A waltz, but a thin and ghostly one. The first violin plays the four-note signature as a dance tune, high and brittle, while the lower instruments thump out the beat.

stops.hear: A high, wiry violin tune in waltz time over a plain oom-pah in the lower instruments
stops.happening: The signature turned into a waltz

stops.hear: The tune passes to other instruments; a sharp little figure appears in the lower strings
stops.happening: A quotation from his First Cello Concerto, written the year before

stops.hear: The waltz returns, quieter and more distant
stops.happening: The dance fades like a memory

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Soft, held notes lead straight into the next slow movement
stops.happening: No pause

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: Three loud, violent chords interrupt a held note, again and again, like knocking at a door. In between, two quotations: a Russian revolutionary funeral song, and a love song from his own opera *Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District*, the work that had brought down Stalin’s anger on him in 1936.

stops.hear: Three sharp, loud chords, repeated, over one held note
stops.happening: The “knocks”. Listeners hear knocks at the door, or bombs

stops.hear: Quiet. A slow, mournful song in the upper instruments
stops.happening: “Tormented by Grievous Bondage”, a Russian revolutionary song of mourning

stops.hear: The knocks return
stops.happening: The threat comes back

stops.hear: The cello, very high in its range, sings a tender, aching melody
stops.happening: Katerina’s aria “Seryozha, my love” from *Lady Macbeth*

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The four notes, quietly, leading into the last movement
stops.happening: The signature again

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: The last movement mirrors the first: the four notes enter one instrument at a time, slower and greyer than before. The quartet ends as it began, in near silence.

stops.hear: The cello starts the four notes; the others enter one by one
stops.happening: Another [[fugato|fugato]] on the signature

stops.hear: A short phrase passes from one instrument to another
stops.happening: A motif from *Lady Macbeth* returns, transformed

stops.hear: The four lines weave together, soft and veiled
stops.happening: The farewell

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: A long, very quiet held chord that fades away
stops.happening: The end

notice: Compare the first and last minutes of the quartet. The same four notes open and close it, first as a question, at the end as a farewell.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The Pavel Haas Quartet, from Prague, recorded the quartet in 2019. The album was named Recording of the Year at the Classic Prague Awards.

threads.title: A signature
threads.body: The four notes of DSCH appear in every movement, in every mood.

threads.title: Memories
threads.body: Quotations from his symphonies, the Piano Trio, the Cello Concerto and *Lady Macbeth* pass by like scenes from a life.

threads.title: Four voices
threads.body: Listen for who leads: the cello opens and closes the quartet, the first violin carries the dances, and at the climaxes all four play as one.
